messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Eigen::Maps
parts:
Will Eigen::Map objects copy into proper Eigen objects?
For example, are these valid?

void function1(const vector<T>& input, vector_t& output) {
output = Eigen::Map<vector_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

vector_t function2(const vector<T>& input) {
return Eigen::Map<vector_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: Eigen::Maps
parts:
Also, are all of our matrix ordering conventions consistent?
Is

matrix_t function2(const vector<T>& input) {
return Eigen::Map<matrix_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

safe, or do we have a better way of turning an STL vector
into an Eigen matrix?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Re: Eigen::Maps
parts: Yes

> On Jul 6, 2015, at 11:26 AM, Michael Betancourt <betan...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Also, are all of our matrix ordering conventions consistent?

Yes, all the external interfaces use Eigen's default of column-major.
To change that, you need to specify more template args, which we
just let default to column major.

> Is
>
> matrix_t function2(const vector<T>& input) {
> return Eigen::Map<matrix_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
> }
>
> safe, or do we have a better way of turning an STL vector
> into an Eigen matrix?

I don't think that'll work.

1. You need rows and columns to get a matrix_t.

2. Because input is a const reference, I'm not sure you
can pass it to a Map for construction.

If you can pass the const reference (or even if you can't and
have to pass a non-const reference, it'll be safe because all
you do is create the Map which then does a copy on return.

- Bob

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Eigen::Maps
parts:
On Monday, July 6, 2015 at 11:15:42 AM UTC-4, Michael Betancourt wrote:
Will Eigen::Map objects copy into proper Eigen objects?
For example, are these valid?

void function1(const vector<T>& input, vector_t& output) {
  output = Eigen::Map<vector_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

vector_t function2(const vector<T>& input) {
  return Eigen::Map<vector_t>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

Almost. This compiles and runs but I had to add some const qualifiers

#include <Eigen/Dense>
#include <vector>
#include <iostream>

void function1(const std::vector<double>& input, Eigen::VectorXd& output) {
  output = Eigen::Map<const Eigen::VectorXd>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

Eigen::VectorXd function2(const std::vector<double>& input) {
  return Eigen::Map<const Eigen::VectorXd>(&(input[0]), input.size());
}

int main () {
  std::vector<double> in (2,42.0);
  Eigen::VectorXd out(2);
  function1(in, out);
  std::cout << "result of function 1: " << out.transpose() << std::endl;
  std::cout << "result of function 2: " << function2(in).transpose() << std::endl;
  return 0;
}
 
I think those are safe for dynamic-sized Eigen matrices. They only warn about fixed size here

http://eigen.tuxfamily.org/dox/group__TopicStlContainers.html

Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Eigen::Maps
parts:
I'd just use this:

MatrixXd a = Map<MatrixXd>(&v[0], rows, cols);

You need to make sure the input vector v isn't constant, otherwise
I think MatrixXd will have to be const.

It constructs the Map expression template, then immediately copies
into a because of the assignment, so it won't actually modify v.

- Bob
